Stealthy describes someone or something that moves, acts, or operates in a way that is careful not to be seen, heard, or noticed.

When something is stealthy, it is deliberately quiet, hidden, and secretive — designed to avoid attracting any attention whatsoever.

Think of a cat creeping up on a bird. It moves slowly, carefully, without making a single sound. It keeps its body low. It doesn't rush. Every movement is controlled so that the bird doesn't notice it coming. That is stealthy behavior.
What Makes Something "Stealthy"?

For something to be truly stealthy, it usually involves a combination of these qualities:

  • Quietness — making little to no sound
  • Slowness and deliberateness — no sudden, attention-grabbing movements
  • Concealment — staying hidden, in shadows, out of plain sight
  • Intentionality — the avoidance of detection is on purpose, not accidental

This last point is important. Stealthy always implies intent. A person who tiptoes through a dark house so they don't wake anyone up is being stealthy. A mouse that just happens to be small and quiet is not really "stealthy" unless it seems like it is trying not to be caught.
What Can Be Described as Stealthy?

The adjective "stealthy" can describe a wide range of things:

People and animals:
A stealthy spy slips past the guards without anyone noticing. A stealthy wolf approaches its prey without snapping a single twig. A stealthy burglar slides through the dark house without making a sound.

Movements and actions:
A stealthy glance is a quick, secret look — the kind you give when you don't want someone to catch you looking. A stealthy approach means moving toward something carefully so as not to be detected.

Methods and tactics:
A stealthy attack comes without warning because the enemy never knew you were coming. In the military, stealthy operations are missions carried out in secret, with no noise and no visibility.

Technology:
You may hear about "stealth aircraft" — these are planes specifically engineered to avoid being picked up by radar. While "stealth" here is a noun/adjective slightly different in form, the meaning flows from the same idea: invisible to detection.
The Feeling and Tone of the Word

"Stealthy" carries a somewhat secretive and cunning tone. It is not a neutral word. When you call something or someone stealthy, you are usually suggesting that they are:

  • Clever and skilled at concealing themselves
  • Potentially up to something — whether good or bad
  • In control of their movements and aware of their surroundings

Depending on the context, stealthy can have a slightly negative or suspicious connotation — because things that try hard not to be seen often do so for a reason. A stealthy stranger lurking near your door feels threatening. However, stealthy can also feel impressive or admirable — like a highly trained soldier or a skilled hunter who moves without a trace.
Degree of Stealthiness

Like many adjectives, "stealthy" can come in degrees:

  • You can be somewhat stealthy (trying to be quiet but not perfectly so)
  • Very stealthy (nearly impossible to detect)
  • Perfectly stealthy (completely undetected)

You can make it stronger with adverbs: "He moved in an incredibly stealthy manner, slipping past every guard."
Synonyms (Words with Similar Meaning)

Understanding related words helps you feel the full shape of a word:

  • Sneaky — similar, but often implies a more negative or childish kind of secrecy (sneaking cookies from a jar)
  • Furtive — secretive in a guilty, nervous way (a furtive glance over the shoulder)
  • Covert — used more in formal/military contexts (a covert operation)
  • Surreptitious — done quietly and secretly to avoid being noticed (slightly more formal)
  • Silent — only captures the sound aspect, not the full idea of avoiding detection

"Stealthy" sits comfortably among all of these but is the most vivid and descriptive of the group — it paints a clear picture of deliberate, careful, silent movement.
Antonyms (Opposite Words)

• Obvious — easy to see or notice
  • Loud / Noisy — attracting attention through sound
  • Blatant — done openly without any attempt to hide
  • Conspicuous — standing out and drawing attention
Common Collocations (Words Often Used With "Stealthy")

These are words you will frequently see sitting next to "stealthy" in real usage:

  • a stealthy approach
  • a stealthy move
  • a stealthy predator
  • a stealthy glance
  • a stealthy exit (leaving a place without anyone noticing)
  • a stealthy attack
  • stealthy footsteps
Example Sentences (From Simple to Complex)

1. The stealthy cat crept across the floor without making a sound.
  2. She made a stealthy exit from the boring party before anyone could stop her.
  3. The soldier was trained to be stealthy — moving through the jungle without rustling a single leaf.
  4. He cast a stealthy glance at her across the room, hoping she wouldn't notice.
  5. The disease had a stealthy nature — spreading silently through the body for years before showing any symptoms. (Here the word is used metaphorically — even a non-living thing can be "stealthy" if it operates quietly and undetected.)
The Adverb Form

When you want to describe how something is done, you use stealthily (the adverb form).

  • "He moved stealthily through the shadows."
  • "She stealthily reached for the last slice of cake."
Summary in One Sentence

Stealthy means acting or moving in a deliberate, quiet, and careful way so as to avoid being seen, heard, or detected — like a shadow that passes through a room and leaves no trace that it was ever there.
